significance: One of only two surviving pre-Pallava temple sites in Tamil Nadu, begun as a brick shrine and rebuilt in stone around 850 CE under Nandivarman II. Later renovations by Rajaraja Chola and by Krishnadevaraya in 1520 make it a compact record of successive South Indian building phases.
story: The name, meaning the seated lord, is explained by the tradition that Rama sat here in grief and was comforted by Bhumi Devi and Nila Devi fanning him with a palm leaf.
